title: Ezekiel Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 35.

questions.question: To whom did the word of the LORD come in Ezekiel 35:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel
questions.explanation: The verse states that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel (Ezekiel 35:1).

questions.question: Against which location was Ezekiel commanded to set his face and prophesy?
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Seir
questions.explanation: The instruction was to set his face against mount Seir and prophesy against it (Ezekiel 35:2).

questions.question: What did the Lord GOD say He would do to mount Seir?
questions.correctAnswer: Make it most desolate
questions.explanation: God declared He would make mount Seir most desolate (Ezekiel 35:3).

questions.question: What will happen to the cities of mount Seir according to Ezekiel 35?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be laid waste
questions.explanation: The LORD said, 'I will lay thy cities waste,' making them desolate (Ezekiel 35:4).

questions.question: Why was mount Seir judged to have perpetual hatred against Israel?
options: Because they shed the blood of Israel's children by the sword during their calamity
Because they refused to trade with Israel
Because they built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because they shed the blood of Israel's children by the sword during their calamity
questions.explanation: The text states mount Seir had perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel by the sword at their time of calamity (Ezekiel 35:5).

questions.question: True or False: In Ezekiel 35:6, God promises to prepare mount Seir unto peace and mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God says He will prepare mount Seir unto blood, and blood shall pursue it, not peace (Ezekiel 35:6).

questions.question: What will fill the mountains of mount Seir according to Ezekiel 35:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Slain men
questions.explanation: The mountains will be filled with slain men in hills, valleys, and rivers (Ezekiel 35:8).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 35:9 says that the cities of mount Seir will return to their former glory.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse says the cities shall not return but remain perpetual desolations (Ezekiel 35:9).

questions.question: What two nations and countries did mount Seir claim as theirs, according to Ezekiel 35:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: The two nations and countries referred to are the house of Israel and Judah, which mount Seir claimed to possess (Ezekiel 35:10).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35:11, what will God do according to mount Seir’s anger and envy?
options: Judge them and make himself known among Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Judge them and make himself known among Israel
questions.explanation: God promises to judge mount Seir according to their anger and envy and make Himself known among Israel (Ezekiel 35:11).

questions.question: What had mount Seir spoken against the mountains of Israel, as stated in Ezekiel 35:12?
options: That they are laid desolate and given to be consumed
That they are protected by God
That they are full of peace
questions.correctAnswer: That they are laid desolate and given to be consumed
questions.explanation: Mount Seir blasphemed saying the mountains of Israel are laid desolate and given to them to consume (Ezekiel 35:12).

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 35:13, mount Seir boasted against God with their mouth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse confirms mount Seir boasted against God and multiplied their words against Him (Ezekiel 35:13).

questions.question: What will happen to mount Seir when the whole earth rejoices, according to Ezekiel 35:14?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be made desolate
questions.explanation: God declares that when the whole earth rejoices, He will make mount Seir desolate (Ezekiel 35:14).

questions.question: What is the reason given in Ezekiel 35:15 for making mount Seir desolate?
options: Because it rejoiced over Israel’s desolation
Because it built a temple to God
questions.correctAnswer: Because it rejoiced over Israel’s desolation
questions.explanation: God will make mount Seir desolate because it rejoiced at the inheritance of Israel when it was desolate (Ezekiel 35:15).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was told to prophesy against mount Seir because of its hatred towards the children of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to prophesy because mount Seir had perpetual hatred and shed the blood of Israel's children (Ezekiel 35:2,5).

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare for Mount Seir because it has not hated blood, according to Ezekiel 35?
options: Mount Seir will be blessed with peace
Mount Seir will become a city of refuge
Mount Seir will be made prosperous
questions.correctAnswer: Blood shall pursue Mount Seir
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:6 states that since Mount Seir has not hated blood, even blood shall pursue it. This indicates a direct consequence of violence upon them.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35, what will happen to those who pass out and return from Mount Seir?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cut off
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:7 declares that God will make Mount Seir desolate and cut off from it those who pass out and return, emphasizing complete devastation.

questions.question: Where does Ezekiel 35 say the slain men will fill in Mount Seir?
questions.correctAnswer: Mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers
questions.explanation: Verse 8 explains that slain men will fall in the mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers of Mount Seir, showing a widespread judgment.

questions.question: What does God promise about the cities of Mount Seir in Ezekiel 35?
options: They shall be perpetual desolations and shall not return
They will be rebuilt and inhabited again
They will be given to Israel
They will become places of worship
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be perpetual desolations and shall not return
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:9 clearly states that Mount Seir's cities will remain perpetually desolate and not return, showing God's judgment.

questions.question: What did Mount Seir claim about two nations and two countries, according to Ezekiel 35?
options: These two nations and countries shall be theirs to possess
They would serve the LORD faithfully
They would remain neutral in conflict
They would become allies with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: These two nations and countries shall be theirs to possess
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:10 reveals Mount Seir's boast that two nations and two countries would be theirs, despite the LORD being there.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:11 describe God's response to Mount Seir's anger and envy?
options: God will act according to their anger and envy and make Himself known
God will forgive their anger and envy
God will ignore their anger and envy
God will bless them for their anger and envy
questions.correctAnswer: God will act according to their anger and envy and make Himself known
questions.explanation: Verse 11 declares that God will respond to Mount Seir's anger and envy by judging them and making Himself known among the nations.

questions.question: What will Mount Seir learn according to Ezekiel 35:12, after God hears their blasphemies?
questions.correctAnswer: That He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:12 states that Mount Seir will know the LORD after He has heard their blasphemies against Israel's mountains.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 35:13 say about Mount Seir's words against God?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 13 confirms that Mount Seir boasted and multiplied words against God, and He heard them, showing their arrogance.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35:14, what will happen to Mount Seir when the whole earth rejoices?
options: Mount Seir will be made desolate
Mount Seir will lead the rejoicing
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Seir will be made desolate
questions.explanation: Verse 14 promises desolation for Mount Seir concurrent with the earth's rejoicing, highlighting God's justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:15 illustrate God's justice in relation to Mount Seir's rejoicing over Israel's desolation?
options: God will make Mount Seir desolate as they rejoiced over Israel's desolation
God will reward Mount Seir for their joy
God will ignore Mount Seir's rejoicing
God will bless Mount Seir abundantly
questions.correctAnswer: God will make Mount Seir desolate as they rejoiced over Israel's desolation
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states that as Mount Seir rejoiced over Israel's inheritance being desolate, so God will make Mount Seir desolate to demonstrate His justice.

questions.question: What biblical virtue can we learn from Ezekiel 35:6-7 about the consequences of hatred and violence?
options: Hatred and violence lead to pursuing bloodshed upon oneself
Hatred and violence bring peace and reconciliation
Hatred and violence are rewarded by God
Hatred and violence have no consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Hatred and violence lead to pursuing bloodshed upon oneself
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 show that because Mount Seir harbored perpetual hatred and shed blood, blood will pursue them, teaching the consequence of such sin.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trusting God's justice can believers learn from the judgment pronounced on Mount Seir in Ezekiel 35:8-9?
options: God will execute justice and make desolations perpetual for the wicked
God ignores wickedness and allows it to prosper
questions.correctAnswer: God will execute justice and make desolations perpetual for the wicked
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 highlight God's faithful execution of justice by making Mount Seir's desolation perpetual, teaching believers to trust in His righteous judgment.

questions.question: How do verses 10 and 11 together show the relationship between human envy and God's righteous judgment?
options: God judges according to the anger and envy shown by Mount Seir
God is indifferent to human emotions
God encourages envy for His purposes
questions.correctAnswer: God judges according to the anger and envy shown by Mount Seir
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 explain that Mount Seir's envy led to their boasting, and God responds by judging them according to that anger and envy.

questions.question: If a believer is struggling with bitterness towards others, what truth from Ezekiel 35:12-13 can encourage them to trust God’s awareness of such attitudes?
options: God hears all blasphemies and boasts, and will make Himself known in His judgment
God does not notice what people say
questions.correctAnswer: God hears all blasphemies and boasts, and will make Himself known in His judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 remind believers that God hears all words and will act justly, encouraging humility and trust in His righteous judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 35:14, when the entire earth rejoices, God will bless Mount Seir.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:14 states that when the whole earth rejoices, God will make Mount Seir desolate, not bless it.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 35.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35:11, what will the Lord GOD do in response to the anger and envy expressed against the people of Israel?
options: He will judge them and make Himself known among Israel
He will bless them with wealth
He will remove Israel from the land
questions.correctAnswer: He will judge them and make Himself known among Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:11 states that the Lord GOD will act according to the anger and envy used out of hatred and will make Himself known among Israel when He has judged them. This shows divine justice and revelation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 35:12 say the enemies of Israel have done with their words against the mountains of Israel?
options: They have spoken blasphemies and boasted that the mountains are desolate
questions.correctAnswer: They have spoken blasphemies and boasted that the mountains are desolate
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explicitly states that the enemies have blasphemed against the mountains of Israel, claiming they are desolate and given to them to consume, showing arrogance and disrespect.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 35:13, what does God say He has heard from the enemies’ mouths?
options: Boasting and multiplication of words against God
questions.correctAnswer: Boasting and multiplication of words against God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:13 records God’s response that He has heard their boasting and many words spoken against Him, emphasizing their arrogance and blasphemy.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 35:14 when God says, 'When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate'?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: Verse 14 uses irony as a literary device: while the earth rejoices, mount Seir will be made desolate. This contrast highlights divine judgment amid human celebration.

questions.question: Ezekiel 35:15 compares the rejoicing of mount Seir at Israel's desolation to what fate that will befall mount Seir itself?
options: It will be desolate like Israel
It will prosper and conquer Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It will be desolate like Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 15 shows a direct parallel: just as mount Seir rejoiced over Israel’s desolation, so it will face desolation itself, demonstrating divine justice and retribution.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage similarly addresses God's judgment on Mount Seir and Edom, connecting with Ezekiel 35:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 34
questions.explanation: Isaiah 34 also prophesies God's judgment on Edom and Mount Seir, echoing Ezekiel 35’s theme of divine retribution against Edom for their hostility towards Israel.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the phrase 'most desolate' (Hebrew: חרבה) as used in Ezekiel 35:3 and 35:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruined and devastated
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word חרבה (charvah) means 'ruined' or 'devastated,' emphasizing total desolation, consistent with the judgment language in Ezekiel 35:3 and 35:7.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35:10, what claim did mount Seir make regarding the two nations and countries?
options: They would protect the two nations
They would possess the two nations and countries
They would ally with the two nations
They would ignore the two nations
questions.correctAnswer: They would possess the two nations and countries
questions.explanation: Verse 10 records mount Seir’s boast that the two nations and countries would be theirs, even though the LORD was present there, highlighting their arrogance and wrongful claim.

questions.question: Ezekiel 35:6 says 'blood shall pursue thee' because mount Seir has not hated blood. What does this imply about the nature of their violence?
options: They were peaceful and avoided violence
They were indifferent to bloodshed and therefore it will come back upon them
questions.correctAnswer: They were indifferent to bloodshed and therefore it will come back upon them
questions.explanation: The verse implies mount Seir did not hate bloodshed but engaged in violence. Therefore, blood (violent retribution) will pursue them as judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 35:9 promises that the cities of mount Seir will be rebuilt and repopulated after their desolation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:9 clearly states the cities will be perpetual desolations and shall not return, indicating no restoration will occur.

questions.question: True or False: The judgment pronounced on mount Seir in Ezekiel 35 is a form of divine retribution for their hatred and violence against Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:5-7 describes the judgment as a response to mount Seir's perpetual hatred and violence against Israel, affirming divine retribution.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:11 reflect the theme of divine justice seen earlier in the book of Ezekiel?
options: By promising mercy and forgiveness without judgment
By asserting that God will judge enemies according to their anger and envy
questions.correctAnswer: By asserting that God will judge enemies according to their anger and envy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel frequently emphasizes God's justice; verse 11 continues this theme by declaring God will judge mount Seir according to their hostile motives.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God making Himself known through judgment as seen in Ezekiel 35:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:18-20
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18-20 speaks of God's wrath revealed against ungodliness, making His righteousness known through judgment, paralleling Ezekiel 35:11’s theme.

questions.question: What historical context underlies the prophecy against mount Seir in Ezekiel 35?
options: Mount Seir represents Edom, Israel’s longstanding enemy who took advantage during Israel’s calamity
Mount Seir represents Egypt, Israel’s ally
Mount Seir symbolizes Babylon, the captor of Israel
Mount Seir is a metaphor for Israel itself
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Seir represents Edom, Israel’s longstanding enemy who took advantage during Israel’s calamity
questions.explanation: Mount Seir is identified with Edom, a nation known for hostility toward Israel, especially during times of Israel’s suffering, as reflected in Ezekiel 35:5.

questions.question: Ezekiel 35:8 uses vivid imagery about slain men filling the mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers. What literary device is primarily employed here?
questions.correctAnswer: Hyperbole
questions.explanation: The description of slain men filling large and varied geographical features uses hyperbole to emphasize the totality of destruction.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is demonstrated by God's declaration in Ezekiel 35:4 regarding the desolation of Mount Seir?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:4 shows God's justice as He promises to lay the cities of Mount Seir waste and make it desolate because of their actions against Israel. This reveals that God holds nations accountable for their deeds, demonstrating divine justice.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 35:5, what was the reason for God's judgment against Mount Seir?
options: Their perpetual hatred and bloodshed of Israel during Israel's calamity
Their refusal to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Their perpetual hatred and bloodshed of Israel during Israel's calamity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:5 explains that Mount Seir is judged because they had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel by the sword during Israel's time of calamity, which reveals the reason for divine punishment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 35:6 teach about the principle of divine retribution?
options: Bloodshed will be avenged by further bloodshed
God will forget the sins of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Bloodshed will be avenged by further bloodshed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:6 states that since Mount Seir did not hate blood, blood will pursue them, teaching the principle of divine retribution where evil deeds bring corresponding judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:8 symbolize the extent of God's judgment on Mount Seir?
options: Mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers will be filled with slain men
The land will become fertile and prosper
The people will be exiled to Egypt
The cities will be rebuilt with joy
questions.correctAnswer: Mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers will be filled with slain men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:8 vividly portrays God's judgment by declaring that the mountains, hills, valleys, and rivers of Mount Seir will be filled with slain men, symbolizing total devastation.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by God's promise in Ezekiel 35:9 that Mount Seir's cities shall not return?
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of eternal punishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:9 emphasizes perpetual desolation and no restoration of cities, illustrating a form of eternal punishment for persistent rebellion against God.

questions.question: What claim of Mount Seir incited God's judgment according to Ezekiel 35:10?
options: That they would possess the lands of two nations despite God's presence there
That they were chosen by God to rule all nations
That they would build a temple for God
That they would become a peaceful nation
questions.correctAnswer: That they would possess the lands of two nations despite God's presence there
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:10 records the boast of Mount Seir that two nations and countries would be theirs, disregarding God’s presence, which provoked divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:11 reveal God's response to human emotions like anger and envy?
options: God acts according to their anger and envy and makes Himself known through judgment
God ignores human anger and envy
questions.correctAnswer: God acts according to their anger and envy and makes Himself known through judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:11 shows that God will execute judgment in response to the anger and envy shown by Mount Seir, making Himself known among the judged, indicating God's righteous sovereignty over human passions.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 35:12 teach about God's knowledge of blasphemy and boasting against Him?
options: God hears and knows all blasphemies spoken against Israel's mountains
God is unaware of human speech
God forgets blasphemies after a time
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and knows all blasphemies spoken against Israel's mountains
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:12 affirms that God is fully aware of all blasphemies spoken against the mountains of Israel, demonstrating His omniscience and intolerance for rebellion.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Ezekiel 35:5-6 and Ezekiel 35:11 provide about divine justice and human sin?
options: God's justice punishes persistent hatred and bloodshed by enacting judgment that reflects human anger and envy
God does not respond to human sin
God forgives all sins without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice punishes persistent hatred and bloodshed by enacting judgment that reflects human anger and envy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:5-6 show God's judgment on hatred and bloodshed, while 35:11 shows God responding to anger and envy with judgment, together teaching that God's justice rightly addresses human sin and emotions.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is evident from the combination of Ezekiel 35:9 and Ezekiel 35:15 about the fate of the enemies of Israel?
options: The doctrine of divine retribution and irreversible judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine retribution and irreversible judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:9 speaks of perpetual desolations and 35:15 declares desolation upon Mount Seir, affirming irreversible divine retribution against those who rejoice over Israel’s ruin.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 35:14 contribute to the narrative arc of God's judgment in the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: God’s judgment on enemies coincides with the earth’s rejoicing, showing His ultimate sovereignty
God’s judgment is unrelated to the earth’s condition
God’s judgment is a private matter
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment on enemies coincides with the earth’s rejoicing, showing His ultimate sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:14 connects God's judgment with the rejoicing of the whole earth, illustrating the theme of God’s sovereign justice celebrated in the eschatological hope of redemption.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Ezekiel 35:7-8 offer to sceptics who claim that divine justice is arbitrary and indiscriminate?
options: God’s justice is targeted and specific, bringing desolation to Mount Seir because of their bloodshed and hostility
God punishes everyone equally without cause
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is targeted and specific, bringing desolation to Mount Seir because of their bloodshed and hostility
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:7-8 demonstrates that God’s judgment is not arbitrary but specifically directed at Mount Seir for their violence and hatred against Israel, affirming purposeful divine justice.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly revealed in Ezekiel 35:13 where God declares He has heard the boasting and multiplied words against Him?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omniscience
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:13 reveals God’s omniscience as He declares that He has heard all the boasting and multiplied words against Him, emphasizing His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: How does the combined teaching of Ezekiel 35:3 and Ezekiel 35:15 shape our understanding of God’s sovereignty over nations?
options: God sovereignly directs the fate of nations, making Mount Seir desolate to declare His lordship
God has no control over nations’ destinies
Nations act independently of God’s will
God only cares for Israel’s fate
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs the fate of nations, making Mount Seir desolate to declare His lordship
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:3 and 35:15 together show that God actively stretches out His hand against Mount Seir and makes it desolate, demonstrating His sovereign authority over all nations.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 35:2 teach about the role of the prophet in relation to God's judgment?
options: The prophet is commanded to set his face and prophesy directly against the enemy
The prophet offers only comfort and no judgment
The prophet negotiates peace without divine instruction
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet is commanded to set his face and prophesy directly against the enemy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:2 commands the prophet to set his face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it, emphasizing the prophetic role in declaring God’s judgment.
